verdict: S1: ART NOT PASS — technically clean, visually insignificant. S2 not generated.
summary: S1 passes every geographic gate under the declared R-B trial: raise-only, 1 965 crest cells and 22 631 shoulder cells each declared, max +20.0 m, summit 197 m and trails 137.8 m from the nearest change, no new sinks, no drainage-destination change, water, coast, beds, corridors, zones and route centrelines unchanged, deterministic.

Artistically it does not change the mountain. From Birchwood and the Central Valley shoulder, the two views that define North Peak's identity, the skyline moves by 4.2 px and 2.7 px. That is visible only in a flicker comparison. The arms do not read as three different profiles but as the same arms with small humps added. The clearest change, about 15 px on the western coast, is a soft lift of the west-spur saddle, which is one camera. Where the raises can be seen at all (south-east oblique, High Tarn east shore), they read as isolated bumps, not as a coherent massing, and the destination-preserving attenuation leaves a hook-shaped dent on the south-east oblique.

Under the brief's stop rules S1 triggers four: the forms remain visually insignificant, only one camera clearly improves, the +25 m envelope is insufficient for the far silhouette, and a meaningful result would require changes to the summit zone, the trail corridor and the crest lower bound. S2 (cut-and-fill) was therefore not generated: it would need lowering below the crest lower bound and editing inside the same frozen zones, which is outside the authorization.
questions: 1. Visibly meaningful from the identity views?

No. Birchwood 4.2 px maximum skyline shift (2.2° of width over 3 px), Central Valley shoulder 2.7 px (none over 3 px), High Tarn overlook 1.1 px, north shore 0.1 px. Even the +25 m upper bound, with every eligible point lifted the full amount and no hydrology guarantees, gives only 9.3 px and 7.6 px from those two far views: at 2.5–2.9 km, 25 m subtends 0.5–0.6°.
2. Are the three arms legibly asymmetric?

No. The A2 shoulder (n-main crest raised at most +13.7 m) and the A1 steps (+17 m on n-crown) start 200–230 m from the summit and are invisible in the far views. The A3 spur shoulder is legible only from the western coast. Without changing the summit block, the arms keep the same symmetric fall from the dome.
3. Does it read as one mountain system?

Not more than M0. The raises are six separate patches. They cannot connect to the summit because the summit is frozen within 150 m (zero change, 80 m fade), and the A3 west arm is frozen along the peak-ascent corridor (zero within ~139 m). So any massing reads as bumps on arms, not as arms growing out of a sculpted summit.

Measured as smooth (fade gradient ≤ core, curvature ≤ core), but not visually clean. Keeping every R1 drainage destination forces local attenuation where a raised crest would shift a divide, and that leaves dents in the raise of up to 11.4 m below the designed surface (693 cells more than 2 m below it). One shows as a hook-shaped notch on the south-east oblique.
5. Does more than one camera improve?

No. Only the western windward coast shows a change that could be called massing (14.9 px, 40° of width over 3 px). From the south-east oblique and the High Tarn east shore, the change is visible but reads as lumps. Elsewhere it is not visible.

Yes, by construction: a flow-preserving cap and destination-preserving attenuation keep every cell above its R1 receiver and every catchment on its R1 destination (0 new sinks, 0 rerouted cells). That validity is exactly what limits the form: on these arms, crest lines are 1–3 cells off the R1 divides, so any visible crest raise moves a divide.
s2: Not generated. The brief says not to proceed automatically if S1 fails, and S1 fails artistically for structural reasons that S2 shares: the frozen summit dome and corridor, the crest lower bound (cut-and-fill needs lowering), and the 25 m envelope at 2.5–3 km distance.
limitations: Clay renders only (two sun presets); no vegetation, snow or atmospheric perspective, which in the shipped look would reduce the visibility of 2–15 px changes further.
Skyline and viewshed measures are terrain-only ray casts on the 4 m grid; the pixel figures assume the review frame (60° vertical FOV, 800 px).

The two new A1c cameras (western coast K3, High Tarn east shore) were chosen to show the arms that the review cameras miss; the western coast frame is dominated by a near foreground slope, which is what a player there sees.

S1 is one parameterisation. Different segment choices within the same rules were tested per segment for hydrology (EA hump 2 dropped, starts moved out of the summit fade). The feasibility upper bound shows no choice within the envelope could reach a strong far-view result.
recommendation: Stop local calibration of North Peak under the current protections. A1a (ridges, invisible), A1b-α (face detail, surface marks) and A1c S1 (crest massing, insignificant) bracket the space: the protected summit dome, the trail corridor on the A3 arm and the crest lower bound together fix the silhouette.

The smallest design-authority change that can produce a different mountain is an R-C revision of the North Peak block in the design master: a re-authored summit block and arm profiles, with summit position and height kept, allowing the crest within ~150 m of the summit to change by up to about ±50–60 m and allowing lowering (saddles, notches) below the current crest bound on the A1 and A2 arms. It must be combined with R-A on the A3 arm only, re-aligning or narrowing the peak-ascent corridor locally so the trail ridge can take a profile, and accompanied by regenerating R1 drainage for the block instead of preserving every current divide.

Before that, an art review should decide what North Peak should look like from Birchwood and the Central Valley shoulder (a target silhouette drawing). The measurements show that the rest of the dossier follows from that one decision.
